name: Priya Menon
title: Rotis that taste like my mother’s
body: I switched from a supermarket 10 kg sack and the difference was immediate — nuttier dough, phulkas that balloon without a fight. We now subscribe to the 5 kg pack.

name: Arjun Deshpande
title: Finally, atta my son will eat
body: We cook together on Sundays. The dough is easier for small hands, and leftover rotis stay soft in the tiffin. Freshness date on the pack actually means something.

name: Neha Kapoor
title: Multigrain that still rolls
body: Every other multigrain atta I tried cracked on the belan. This one rests well and makes a slightly darker, very soft roti. The 5 kg is good value.

name: Farhan Qureshi
title: Pakoras with a proper chana smell
body: The besan is finer than village mill stuff but still fragrant. Kadhi came out silkier. Will reorder with the atta subscription.

name: Sonal Iyer
title: Quiet, clean flavour
body: Not dramatically different from the classic pack, but I like knowing the farm story. Packaging arrived intact in the Chennai heat — tin it the same day.

name: Lakshmi Nair
title: Ragi porridge the children actually finish
body: Malty, not bitter. I mix a spoon into wheat atta for dinner rotis. Please never roller-mill this.

name: Vikram Singh
title: Tastes like home in winter
body: Bought from the Sitapura mill pickup. Bajra was ground that morning. Raab and thick rotis — this is the real grain, not the bitter flour from the kirana.

name: Meera Joshi
title: Good bhakri flour
body: Needs warm water and a firm hand, as jowar should. Fresh pack, no aftertaste. Would love a 5 kg option.
